short: Richard Hakluyt was a writer and geographer whose works tirelessly promoted the English colonisation of North America.
full:
Born around 1552, Richard Hakluyt became an ordained minister and one of the era's pre-eminent geopolitical strategists. He systematically compiled translated accounts of European voyages, networking extensively with sea captains and merchants to document the practical geography of the New World.

His major work, Principal Navigations, Voiages, Traffiques and Discoueries of the English Nation, argued passionately that England needed to expand its maritime presence to counter Spanish dominance and relieve domestic poverty. His intellectual groundwork directly inspired the chartering of early commercial companies and motivated figures like Walter Raleigh, establishing the ideological blueprint for the British Empire.
